name: Professional services
title: New capability. The same duty of care.
intro: Practical AI education for firms whose work depends on judgement, quality and client trust.
problem: Research, drafting and internal knowledge work can be useful places to explore AI. But a plausible answer is not enough when people rely on the result. The approach needs to fit the standards your firm already works to.
useCases: Research & synthesis
Develop a repeatable way to prepare research briefs from approved sources, with source checking and clear limitations.
First drafts & review
Give people a useful starting structure while preserving professional judgement, review and authorship.
Internal knowledge
Explore how colleagues can find and use approved information without ignoring access or maintenance.
boundary: Professional review remains with your firm. We do not provide legal, accounting or regulated advice, and training does not certify a workflow as compliant.

name: Sales & client teams
title: Better prepared. More present.
intro: Help client-facing teams use AI for the work around a conversation, without losing the human relationship.
problem: Preparation, account context and follow-through can consume attention that belongs with the customer. The aim is not to automate trust. It is to help people arrive informed and leave with a clear next step.
useCases: Account preparation
Build a grounded briefing using relevant, approved information rather than a generic summary.
Proposal preparation
Turn a clear brief and known requirements into a draft that still receives a person’s review.
Follow-through
Make ownership and next actions explicit after the conversation. Keep records useful and accurate.
boundary: No invented personalisation, fabricated familiarity or autonomous promises to customers. People remain accountable for the communication they send.

name: Operations teams
title: Less friction. More considered work.
intro: Explore AI at the level where it has to earn its place: the actual workflow.
problem: Operational work is rarely just the neat task in a demonstration. It includes checks, exceptions, workarounds and transfers between systems. Those are part of the design, not details to discover later.
useCases: Recurring reporting
Define the sources, quality threshold and review needed to make a recurring summary useful.
Enquiry triage
Explore bounded categorisation and routing, with explicit exceptions and a clear owner.
Knowledge handoffs
Document the context and instructions another person needs to carry the work forward.
boundary: Start with a baseline and a bounded pilot. Production access, integrations, hosting and ongoing support require an explicit implementation scope.

name: Learning & development
title: Learning that stays with the team.
intro: Role-specific AI education that connects a session to observable capability at work.
problem: A full training room is not the same as a more capable team. Relevance, practice, feedback and follow-through need as much care as the presentation.
useCases: A shared starting point
Understand differences in access, confidence and experience without ranking people with an artificial AI score.
Practice that matters
Use safely selected tasks and examples from the team’s context. Make time for people to try, question and revise.
A meaningful review
Agree what participants should be able to do afterwards, and review actual work alongside their feedback.
boundary: The programme is practical professional development, not an accredited qualification. Measures are agreed with the sponsor and used to improve learning, not surveil individuals.
